capabilities.target: executive's Drive (board materials, draft financial results)
any recipient, from the executive's mailbox
executive's calendar (accept invite) and triggers document search plus email drafting

inputs.source: Calendar invite with free-text description, sendable by anyone including outside the company

instructions.note: "find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees" places no limit on document sensitivity searched or on who the attendees may be, including the invite's own (unverified) sender.
The only constraint on accept-and-send behavior is the prompt's wording; no structural gate (approval, recipient restriction, content filter) is described anywhere in the design.

"Act on invites as they arrive" grants the agent standing authority to use the executive's mail and drive credentials in response to content written entirely by the invite's sender, who is not authenticated as the executive.

elements.name: Any invite sender, internal or external, not authenticated to the agent
Agent-authored daily summary reviewed by the executive

controls.name: Daily summary reviewed by the executive
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is written by the same agent that performed the actions, after the actions (including the email send) have already completed. A more capable or compromised model writes a more persuasive and more selectively incomplete summary that hides an injected action (ASI09), and review is after the fact, not preventive.

controls.name: Human approval, raw action review, before sending to any non-company recipient
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model at the point mail.send is invoked, checking the recipient domain against a company allowlist. It works regardless of model capability unless the gate itself is removed or its volume grows unreviewable.

controls.name: Independent, tamper-evident action log
controls.decay_rationale: A log written by the orchestration layer, not by the model, stays attributable regardless of what the model later reports in its own summary.

controls.name: Injection classifier on invite descriptions
controls.decay_rationale: A separate classifier screening invite text for embedded instructions does not scale with the primary agent's capability; multi-step, encoded, or long-horizon payloads can get past it.

controls.name: Restrict unattended drive access to meeting-relevant, non-restricted documents
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scope enforced by the drive service itself does not depend on model behavior; the model cannot read what the credential cannot reach.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): injected calendar invite drives confidential document read and unrestricted external email send

attack_path.note: Anyone, including outside the company, can send an invite with a free-text description.
Agent accepts the invite and begins the prepare step driven by the invite's free-text content.
Agent searches and reads the executive's Drive, including board materials and draft financial results, to find 'related documents.'
Agent emails a brief, which can include confidential content, to the invite's attendees, with no recipient restriction and no approval step.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Already at the ceiling with no preventive controls in place. Watch for any later-added safeguard (recipient allowlist, approval gate) being disabled via config change, or for autonomy/step limits being loosened further, which would widen blast radius even though the tier cannot rise further.

evidence.observation: "Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite. The invite description is free text written by the sender."
"For each new invite, accept it if the time is free, then prepare: find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees." The invite content, not a vetted task, drives the search and send.
"The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results." and "mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step."

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw action review (full recipient list and document list shown, not a summary) before mail.send delivers to any recipient outside the verified company domain.
Scope drive.search_and_read so unattended invite-triggered searches cannot reach board materials or draft financial results; require elevated approval for access to restricted-tier documents.

Treat invite descriptions as untrusted data: never let free-text invite content select which documents to retrieve or determine outgoing email content; spotlight/delimit invite text away from task instructions.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions (repudiation): only a self-written daily summary

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor for any claim that the daily summary has been upgraded to an independent, tamper-evident audit log. Until that exists, increased autonomy or further control removal keeps accountability at the same gap.

evidence.observation: "The daily summary is written by the agent itself." No independent or tamper-evident record of accept/read/send actions is described.
"Act on invites as they arrive; the executive reviews a daily summary." Review is after the fact and relies entirely on the agent's own account.

recommendations.action: Write every accept, search, and send action to an independent, tamper-evident audit log maintained by the orchestration layer, separate from the agent-authored daily summary shown to the executive.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe how the executive's chat channel authenticates requests, so whether the executive could be spoofed via that channel is not assessed here.
Artifacts do not describe whether invite sender identity is logged or linked to calendar provider authentication records, so repudiation risk for the sending entity itself cannot be assessed.
This flow carries inbound invite content only; it does not carry outbound confidential data, so disclosure risk is assessed on the outbound mail flow instead.
No in-transit tampering of the outgoing message is evidenced by the design; the material risk is disclosure of agent-chosen confidential content, not alteration of the message.
The daily summary is reviewed only internally by the executive and is not transmitted externally in this design, so it does not itself serve as a disclosure channel.
The daily summary is a simple internal digest with no processing loop or resource constraint that an external actor could exploit to cause denial of service.

rating.rationale: The design lets anyone who can send the executive a calendar invite drive a chain of confidential document retrieval and unrestricted external email send, with no approval step, no recipient restriction, and no content classifier on the invite text (TC1 lethal trifecta). No structural control covers this path today, so residual risk equals inherent risk at critical. The only existing control, a daily summary, is detective, self-authored by the agent, and reviewed after the email has already been sent, so it earns no tier credit and also leaves agent actions without an independent, attributable record (property finding f2, capped at high). Because no mitigating control yet exists, the forecast cannot be defeated further by a trigger and stays at critical; closing the gap requires adding, not just weakening, structural controls such as a raw-action approval gate on external sends, scoped drive access, and an independent audit log.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope such as exact drive and mailbox credential scope is inferred from the runtime notes rather than verified, which limits confidence on credential_scope values to medium.
No detail is given on how the executive's own chat channel is authenticated to the agent, so spoofing risk on that channel is not assessed.
